As best I can tell, the Kindle Fire version will go no further than Level 35, at least not without paying 99 cents to unlock the next set of levels.  Let's see: 440 levels @ .99 cents per 35 levels = $12.57.  Kinda pricey for an app, particularly when you consider how many match-3-type games are out there.  It would be nice to know what the pricing structure was--I could see paying $1.99 or even $2.99 for a game where all levels were theoretically accessible, even if in-app purchases continued to be available.<br /><br />Obviously, it *IS* possible to solve the initial puzzles without purchasing extra lives, moves, or boosters.  It remains to be seen whether this is true at higher levels--and I imagine it's not something I'm going to ever find out.<br /><br />Perhaps if I were in the Facebook majority (seems to be a requisite for this game), it would be more appealing.  As it is, I find it appalling from an ethical point of view, and diabolically clever from a MBA's point of view.  After all, fools and their money deserve to be parted. And who am I to say whether or not people are getting their dollar's -worth of utility each time they choose to cheat at a video game?<br /><br />10/28/2013 UPDATE<br />A kind commenter pointed out that it's possible to unlock the next set of levels by successfully completing \\"Mystery Quests\\"--in the case of level 35 and 50, there are 3 \\"quests\\" (which are just like game levels). The next quest becomes available 24 hours after successfully completing the one before.  The first set of quests unlocks the levels up to 50--meaning that you can rack up quite a bill if you're impatient and pay to unlock levels. (440-35=405; 405/15 = 27; $26.73).  You can therefore view \\"pay to play\\" as payment in money or incovenience.  Pick your poison.<br /><br />What seems to make Candy Crush different from other match-3 games (e.g., Bejeweled, Jewel Star; former FAOTD \\"Around the World in 80 Days,\\" Heroes of the Kalevala,\\" and \\"Call of Atlantis\\"), otherthan the social-network connections (and associated peer pressure) are fairly trivial:<br />1) On most levels, the limiting factor is MOVES, not time. One can contemplate the position of the pieces at leisure and find and plan for 4- and 5-piece matches.<br />2) The special tiles resulting from 4- and 5-pieces matches (roughly equivalent to bombs and lighting bolts in similar games) can be combined for an amplified effect.<br />3) When there are moves left over after achieving the goal of a level, the game goes into a hypnotic autoplay mode in which it simulates the effects of special tiles and adds thousands of points to the score for that level.<br /><br />There's a moral in there somewhere, but I don't know what it is.<br /><br />P.S. Does it look to you as if developers are not only paying for reviews, they're also paying for those reviewers to mark all 5-star reviews as \\"helpful\\" whether they are or not?  I hope this can be reined in before the review system is rendered completely unhelpful.

Candy Crush is an addicting puzzle game.  It's easy to learn and the controls on a tablet are simple.  This just recently became available for the Kindle Fire HD, and it works flawlessly.  The game looks and sounds great; although the music loops can get annoying, and after a while I prefer to play with the sound off.<br /><br />The only issue I have with the game is that some levels are very difficult and you can get stuck on the same level for quite some time.  Furthermore, you only have 5 \\"lives\\", and once you're out you have two options... pay 99 cents for +3 lives (no thanks), or simply wait -- the game credits you one life every 30 minutes.  So you can either fork over your hard-earned money, or you'll have to go do something else while you wait for your lives to replenish.  I just opt to wait, but it kills the momentum.<br /><br />So at times it does get frustrating, and there are too many occasions where the game developers ask you to purchase an add-on (which is understandable given that the game itself is a free download).  But overall, this is the most fun tablet-based game I've played.

I love match three games and download every free (and many pay) game I can find.  I try them ALL out.  This has to be the WORST I've encountered and I'm shocked because everyone raves about it.  I think this must simply be because people have not found the many highly superior (many Candy themed) match 3 games out there that are TRULY FREE or very inexpensive to play.  This game not only looks pretty shabby (for a beautiful spectacular looking Candy match 3 game check out the free Candy Deluxe Pro available free here on Amazon) but it is also so limiting in what it allows you to do that it literally becomes unplayable.  Don't want to wait for two and a half hours when you run out of your very limited 5 lives?  PAY US MONEY or log onto Facebook and spam your friends.  Once you reach level 35 the game is truly desperate to get your money so it will not allow you to move to the next level until you pay the ransom or play 3 \\"quests\\" which are merely levels you have already played. Okay, I can do that.  Play and beat the first \\"quest\\" level and guess what?  You may not play again for 24 hours to do the second quest!  When you beat that one you wait ANOTHER 24 hours to play the final one.  This is the only game I have ever played that prohibits you from playing the game.  It isn't really much of a game either as it is deliberately and obviously rigged in much the same ways as a carny hucksters game.  You will NOT beat a level until the game decides that you will (generally when you are using your final life - a cynical ploy to get you to pay for more lives).  Level design is also so difficult that in advanced levels you will almost certainly have to pay for (outrageously expensive) \\"boosters\\" to move on.<br /><br />I really don't get it.  The only explanation for the popularity/social phenomenon nature of this game is that people have not played the MANY better ones.  For awesome Candy themed match 3 games try: CANDY DELUXE PRO, CANDY SWIPED, CANDY OF KING, MO CANDY (thatone is 99cents), CANDY POP. For great match 3's in general try JEWEL STAR, JEWEL LEGENDS, DRAGON GEM, HEROES of KALEVALA, SEASONS MATCH ... so many great ones.  The ones that require you to pay (cheap too) give you the ENTIRE game, not just pay to progress a little further and then pay again. The fawning reviews here mystify me, particularly the ones that seem so happy the game is \\"finally\\" available on Amazon.  The reason the game took so long to come out is so the game will get a huge new influx of players to make it seem like interest in the game is not diminishing (which it does do fairly quickly, at least for my friends who have tried it and quit playing it when in became annoying).  CANDY CRUSH is a truly disappointing and I think, rather despicable mess.

I love candy crush saga!!! This is another one of those games where you Match three of more of the same thing and you get points and more fall down. But it has many unique features that make it different than all the rest. When you Match four of the same candy you get a a special striped candy. When you Match that one it clears a whole row of candy. When you Match five of the same color you get a chocolate candy. When you Match this with another candy all of that color disappears. There are also wrappers candies that clear all of the candies around it. There are also goals for each level. For example one is getting a cherry down to the bottom of the screen by matching the candy below it causing it to fall down. I will not explain all of them but you can find out on your own :). There are lots of cool features and other stuff in this app and I recommend this app to anyone especially to anyone who's a fan of this kind of game. The only thing that I don't like is that it can be really frustrating sometimes. For example right now I am stuck on level 27. I can not pass this level for the life of me!!! And you also have lives. When you lose a level, you lose a life. Once you lose all five lives up you have to wait to play again. Over all this app is pretty good. But if you don't have a lot of patience, this can sometimes be really frustrating.<br />Hope this review helped!!:) -izzy

Love this game &amp; hate this game. This is not your typical match 3 game. There are challenges that can be rather frustrating, but hey, isn't that the purpose. I never play match 3 games because they've become boring &amp; predictable. This game is neither! The more advanced you go in the game, the harder the levels become. Don't expect to breeze through like you would on other match 3 games. Update 12/6/2013<br />I originally gave this game a two-star rating because I was stuck at level 30 and felt there'd be no way to continue without paying for boosts, which are ridiculously expensive for one-time use. However, after persisting for days - maybe after 30 or so attempts, I finally got past it. After that, each level has been challenging but not impossible. I was again stuck for days on level 70, but finally got through it. At certain levels, you have to finish three quests in order to continue and you have to wait 24 hours between each quest. It can be frustratingly difficult at times and a lot depends more on luck rather than skill, but now I know it's not impossible, I enjoy the challenge. I think what makes this game more satisfying than some of the other match-3 games is the animations and sound effects of crushing multiple rows of candy.<br /><br />Original post:<br />I downloaded this game on my Kindle Fire HD because a colleague of mine was playing it on her phone during breaks (she said \\"Candy Crush\\" so I'm assuming it's the same game) and says she's absolutely addicted. I play all sorts of puzzle games, and have enjoyed many of the match-3 games. Compared with some of the other match-3 games I've played, this one is very basic. The graphics are fine and I expect quite appealing to people who love candy but they are not in any way sophisticated and there is no point except to get to higher levels. Even though you earn points as part of the game, earning them is meaningless because you can't use them for anything.<br />The biggest problem is, once you hit a certain level, there doesn't seem to be any way of advancing without spending money to buy boosters - which are not cheap at all. I had fun for a little while but started to get frustrated when I got to levels where if I failed I had to wait or spend money in order to continue playing. Still, I could live with waiting since I have many other games to keep me busy. However, I have not been able to get beyond Level 30 in spite of retrying it at least 20 or 30 times. In this game, you have to drop all the ingredients (cherries and nuts) to the bottom. The lower part of the board is initially filled with the \\"cement\\" tiles that have to be broken before they can be put into play. Even if you manage to smash all the cement tiles and drop the ingredients to the bottom, not all the ingredients are on the board until there are very few moves left. Maybe it's possible to clear this level if you get very lucky, but after trying it so many times I've come to the conclusion there's no way to get beyond this level without spending money on boosters. The price for the boosters (for this particular level) is 99cents for 5 extra move and 3 hammers - which is ridiculously expensive because they would get used up really fast. (You're initially given some boosters when you win some levels to give you an idea of what they do.) I wouldn't spend any money on this game anyway, but a one-time purchase of a dollar or two in order to be able to win boosts within the game might be reasonable.<br />Although I wouldn't call it \\"absolutely awful\\" because the game works as intended, I agree with Gregorio who pointed out that there are so many better games of a similar ilk out there that don't try to force you to spend money. I prefer the games where there's some back story and clearing each level results in achieving some objective, such as Heroes of Kalevala and Azkend2. The graphics are gorgeous in these games. They are paid apps but I downloaded them as the FAOTD. But there are also many free games out there that might ask you to pay for an ad-free version or for boosts to help speed up your progress, but which don't make it altogether impossible to progress.<br /><br />Update 11/03/2013 I FINALLY got past level 30 but I don't know how many times I had to attempt it.to get beyond Level 30 in spite of retrying it at least 20 or 30 times. I've been waiting for Candy Crush to come out on the Kindle market. My older sister owns it and is on level 170 or something. Having recently bought it, I'm on 35, but I do know a lot about the game.<br />  Candy Crush has great graphics and somewhat of a storyline. You are helping a little girl find her way through the world of candy crush, while helping the &quot;owner&quot; of a specific section. With about 10 or 12 levels per section, you have five lives. When you beat a level, that life is not taken from you. When you finish a section, with the exception of the first two sections, you must complete three quests that are 24 hours apart.<br />  Candy Crush does have a lot of in-game buying. Yes, it's trying to cheat you out of your money. But keep in mind that the game is free; they have every right to try. I know I would rather buy a free game with a lot of in-game buying options than a paid game with none. With in-game buying, you can play the game ans choose to spend your money, but you don't have to. That's another thing: the game does not need money to continue game-play. Game-play is completely free. Help with game-play is not.<br />  Most of the bad reviews for this game are complaining about the in-game buying. These people seem to have no patience. With patience, this game is great! However, some people just end up paying because they can't wait. That's what the game is counting on.<br />So, to recap, this game is well-worth your non-money, and, if you decide to do in-game buying, your few dollars. Have fun!

The first 10 levels are very easy and you advance to next level easily.<br /><br />After that, levels/boards are much harder and extremely frustrating. You can be stuck on one level for days. I like a challenging game but this is ridiculous. Also, I've noticed that the level's board changes with every replay. It's not like you are getting a chance to change some of the moves you made in the previous game. It is very frustrating. It is not my idea of fun or enjoyment.<br /><br />Also, the game initially provides you with \\"gold bars & special boosters\\" to help you. However, once you've used your free gold bars & boosters, you cannot get more unless you pay for them with real money. I am NOT going to spend money to play this game! Another thing I don't like is that you only get 5 lives per game session. Once you've lost your 5 lives, you cannot play again for a certain period of time. Why should I have to wait 30 minutes or an hour or more to continue playing? And again here, you can skip the wait and buy more lives for $.<br /><br />The last thing I dislike about this game is the Facebook \\"share\\" aspect of it.  Ask your friends for help. Ask your friends to send you extra moves or an extra life.  Share with your friends that you conquered a level etc. No, I don't want to ask my friends. No, I don't want to boast that I beat my friends' score; I JUST WANT TO PLAY A GAME FOR MY OWN FUN AND ENTERTAINMENT AND I WANT TO PLAY WHEN I HAVE THE TIME TO PLAY.  I don't want to be told \\"you can't play anymore now, come back later!\\".

Like all good games you don't need to be connected to Wi-Fi to play this so you can play it at home or anywhere you've a little bit of time to kill and not just places with free Wi-Fi.  A lot of others had been playing and mentioning this game, claiming they were addicted and so forth so I decided to check it out. Best to play with the sound on as then you get the old 80's arcade noise game machine experience (or the same sort of noises and lights as your poker machines, but you don't have to feed coins into this).  Eric Cartman may have made the catchphrase Sweeeeeeeeeeeeettttt catchy in the 90's, but the voice in this one has brought that catchphrase back to popular culture as the game praises a nice move you make that causes the disappearance of a lot of fruit.  That's basically the premise of the game, it's a number of challenges where you need to match up three of the same pieces of fruit which make them disappear.  As the levels go up you have missions to achieve such as getting three objects to the bottom of the screen in a set maximum number of moves so it becomes a bit of a mental challenge.<br /><br />The only thing I don't like about this is If you take a while to think about your next move (or something interesting is happening on the TV while your playing) it prompts you with possible moves, I would love to be able to turn that off as it is cheating after all.  Have a button you press to get a hint if you want but the whole point of a mental challenge is to challenge yourself, so the game could do without the hints.<br /><br />Update March 2014 - When I got to level 130 of Candy Crush (in the Water Wharf area of the map) I had no idea what to do as the order to fulfil is five brown striped balls.  First I assumed it meant the blue lollie ones when striped (after four of one candy in a row turns the candy you slid in to striped after the other three disappear), as they resembled the picture just a different colour. That wasn't it. Then I just assumed it was setting of any stripe.  It wasn't in fact I set off about 30 stipes in one game and really couldn't work out how to get these brown striped candy.  But I worked it out and have come back and typed this into my review so if your searching all reviews with the words level 130 or something you'll know how to do it.<br /><br />What you need to do to win Candy Crush's level 130 is line up two of any striped candies either on top or next to each other.  Then you need to smash these two striped candies together (of course doing this takes out the whole line of candies horizontal and vertical when you do).  You need to do this five times in that game to win in addition to getting the minimum score.  So you line up as many four in a rows as possible and try avoid making the chocolate freckle with five (ignore you natural instinct to create the freckle) in a row by dropping one end of the candy first before dropping the fourth into the middle.  Level 130 is actually quite easy once you know what you are supposed to do.<br /><br />Level 131 however has the same concept but is a lot harder, as you've got the game divided into four boxes, one has chocolate in it and the other a bomb that goes off in ten moves.<br /><br />Hope this info helped you to continue on and eased the fear of what am I going to do now, I've become addicted to this game but can't see any possible way to complete level 130 feeling.was setting of any stripe. But that I could give less than a single star.<br /><br />One of the most unfortunate developments in mobile gaming is the proliferation of wait gaming - rather than getting a game and being able to actually play it as much as you like, which would make sense, your ability to play the game itself is crippled. This, by any logic, should be the immediate end of any studio that embraces it. If you bought a car that you could only drive ten miles a day unless you paid to &#34;unlock&#34; additional miles, that car manufacturer wouldn't last the week. But we've come to accept this from games for some reason.<br /><br />Candy Crush Saga is simply a match-three game, a concept that's been around since at least 1990, when Columns was released for the Sega Genesis. Candy Crush Saga takes everything fun about Columns and makes you pay for it, or else wait. Want those special power-ups you're told you earned? Pay. Want to play after losing five times in a row? Pay or wait. Want to play those new levels you just unlocked? Pay or wait three days. King.com stole a game concept and then held the game's enjoyability hostage. There is absolutely nothing new here - every &#34;challenge&#34; is taken from another game that innovated, and cast about in levels that are designed for you to lose. The more you lose, the more you have to wait, the more you (hopefully) pay. The more powerups you (hopefully) buy. The more quests you (hopefully) fork over to skip.<br /><br />This entire concept needs to stop. Unfortunately, until players wise up and stop rewarding studios for doing this, it won't. Perhaps someday.

I'd give it 5 stars for the fun and challenge of the game, but I'm a bit disappointed in their way of making money off the game...far more money than the game SHOULD be worth.  After a number of games, you can go to the next level if you meet 3 challenge games, but you have to wait 24 hours between winning one and the next one.  OR you can fork out $1 to move to the next level.  There are also ways to purchase more lives when you run out (you automatically get a new life every 30 minutes, up to 5) and more special candies to help you win.<br /><br />Now, I really probably shouldn't complain at all, since it is a CHOICE to pay for these extra items. You aren't forced to, and if you're patient, you can just play the challenges until you win and then move the next level and you can play with the lives you have and the candies you're handed.  But you have to be willing to do so.  I would suggest that, if you're someone impatient, who has issues with spending money you shouldn't, don't get Candy Crush, as I imagine your bank account can be severely diminished by it if you allow it.<br /><br />Otherwise, definitely fun and entertaining.

Candy Crush Saga is a fun, and addictive game.  With lots of puzzles, and plenty of challenges, the game is a lot of fun.  However it does have it's flaws.<br /><br />The first flaw is that your limited to 5 lives before having to wait.  The problem here is that if you use your lives, you must wait to play again which can really hurt the flow of gameplay.<br /><br />The second is the reliance of micro transactions.  This is where the game is really hurt.  You see on the higher levels it can get so tough that its easy to be tempted to buy 5 more moves, or power ups which quite frankly can add up really fast.<br /><br />The final issue is the reliance of Facebook.  After a while you'll get to a point where you have to reach out to Facebook friends to continue.  If you don't have 3 friends who are playing, you have to pay to continue.<br /><br />So overall this game is good, but the reliant on micro transactions and facebook hurt it for the long run.

The is a fun and easy to learn game that is good for persons of all ages. It is very similar in game play to Bejeweled. There are many levels to complete, but it should only take 5 minutes at the most to complete any one level, and you are not penalized if you do not. The background music is a little overwhelming, but you can turn it off. The other background sounds are good. However, I can see where playing this game can become addictive so I don't recommend spending more than 15 minutes at a time with it. Also, if you like, there is a Facebook connection tab so you can share your results with others. It also could become &#34;spendy&#34; as you can buy support items to complete a level. The items are not expensive by any means, but the purchases could become an unnecessary habit.<br />Overall, however, this little game is fun and I recommend its purchase.

Candy Crush is a great game, even better than I thought. At first I thought it was just another game like Bejeweled, except with candy, but it's not. While it is a &quot;match-three&quot; game, it's also more. It gives you goals and missions, and if you don't achieve those goals, you can't move on. It gives you five lives, and when you use up those lives, you have to wait, however long, for the next ones. I like the fact that you don't have to wait for all of the lives to play again. Sometimes I get stuck on levels and have to wait, and it's really fun, because when I get past that level I get excited. I would recommend this game!<br /><br />PS: I am GiGi Sparkles, not C. Robson.

Where do I begin?<br />King was absolutely shameful in its marketing tactics for this game. Just like EA, Candy Crush runs on the idea of &quot;free-to-play equals pay-to-win&quot;. Actually, scratch that, because this game isn't even free to play. The levels are designed to be almost impossible, so as to convince you to either A) spam your friends' Facebook accounts with requests for power-ups or extra lives, or B) spend money to be able to win. I've seen my mom play this game, and she's had to retry certain levels more times than she would've bothered to count. Also, at certain points in the game, you get locked out for three days until you either pass the daily challenges (which are just previous levels that you've already beaten) or --surprise, surprise-- buy the privilege to continue onwards. I feel sorry for all the ladies who ruined their credit cards, and their online reputations, by playing this piece of crap. Never before have the limits of human greed been pushed this far.<br /><br />Oh, and as a bonus, it's a shameless ripoff of Bejeweled.

Candy Crush Saga is a fun and entertaining game. I have waited a long time for Amazon to provide a version for the Kindle Fire and am very pleased to finally get it! You do not need access to wi-fi to play this game on your kindle fire but let me say tho that if you play via facebook also, you must have access to wi-fi and log in to facebook from your kindle for the game on your kindle to update to the level you are on via facebook. That doesn't mean you can't play this game if you don't have facebook, it just means if you do and you want to be on the same level you are on when you played on facebook you must log in to facebook for it to sync to the same level. Once you have synced levels you do not need to log in to facebook to play on your device unless you leveled up while playing on facebook and your device does not show that you did. Otherwise you will start at level one on your device whether you play it on facebook or not. For those that get upset on facebook because they want to know what happens to all the 'lives' they were gifted from friends, they will show up in your gift box on your kindle or other device (at least on my iphone they do). They can be used as long as you don't accept them until you need them. In other words if you run out of live's, while on your kindle or iphone, open your gift box on the home page of the game and accept only 5 of the gifted live's at a time. (5 is how many live's you are given per game so accepting more from your gift box will cause you to loose them.)<br />For those that have not played Candy Crush Saga, The game show's up on the screen with varying shaped designs, obstacles and deterrents, in and around them are rows of candies.. orange, blue, green, red (look like jelly beans hence..the candies) on top of square jellies. There are several different challenges but for the most part you are given a certain number of moves, (which vary per level) the general object is to match 3 or more of the same color candies to makethem move or disappear, breaking up the jellies beneath them. Each move will break up the square jellies if there are any still remaining under the ones you have moved, eventually resulting in clearing the board of jellies.<br />Some levels you will be required to clear all the jellies, as well as acquire a certain number of points to be able to move on to the next level. Some are harder than others to achieve both but it can be done!<br />Matching 4 candies will take away 3 but leave you with 1 of the same color that now has stripes (called a 'special' candy) and when matched with 2 or more of that same color will blow out a line of candy, sometimes causing a string of candies to move, taking with it other candies and jellies, which will change the arrangement of candies, sometimes for your benefit, sometimes not!  Sometimes another 'special' candy shows up that is a 'wrapped' candy, matching it up with 2 or more of the same color causes it to blow up the candies around it and then it drops down and blows the candy's around it again, somewhat creating a change in the arrangement of the candies on the board.<br />Matching 5 or more of the same color will get you a multi-colored ball of candy that can help clear out the board if played right. Using the multi-colored ball of candy can be used with 1 of any color candy you wish (as long as it is next to it), creating all of that color candy to become blown off the screen. Combining the multi-colored candy with a 'special' candy will create a different kind of explosion! Learning what each candy can do makes the game work for you, and of course some computer luck will hopefully come along for you too! There are many different challenging levels as you go higher and other objects are added to the challenge to complete the level's.<br />This game is challenging as you get to higher levels, and aggravating sometimes too! Mainly aggravating because certain levels seem near impossible to complete the challenge! The levels can be cleared tho, it takes time. I have never spent money on this game to clear levels. I refuse to play a game that you need to spend your hard earned money on, so if that were to happen I would be done but so far I have had no problem.<br />Sometimes it's just a matter of waiting for the right time (a little luck!) to come along and you complete the level and can move on. Right now I am stuck on level 133 and have been for a few months. This is the first level that has taken me this long, most are cleared in decent time but some are harder to figure out and hence take longer. It is a great time consuming and addicting game. Even if you get frustrated with a level, leave it for a while then come back and chance's are you will complete it soon. My grandchildren love to play this also, (ages 5 & 3) they do pretty well at it. They may not comprehend the object completely but it's exciting for them to 'blow some candies up' and yell &#34;got one gma!&#34; so it is fun for all ages. In my opinion for the younger children it helps with hand-eye coordination too! It's a great, colorful, addicting game for all!  I'm sure I left out many details but for the most part this is a general description of the game! Hope it helps!

After a year or so, I finally caved & downloaded Candy Crush Saga when it became available for the Kindle Fire.<br /><br />When I started playing the game, I understood why everyone I know loves this game. It's colorful, the graphics are so well done that I can almost taste the candy. The sound effects are fun too, but I usually turn  down the volume so I don't disturb my family.<br /><br />I'm addicted to Candy Crush Saga now, but I get perturbed when I can advance by sharing with Facebook friends. I refuse to bother anyone on Facebook & I'm resisting any purchases of boosters that would allow me to continue a game or buy a life. So I'm progressing slowly. When I have to wait  up to 28 minutes for another life, I find something else to do. There have been some levels that I never thought I'd win. I was stuck on a level in the 20's for what seemed like forever & was surprised when I finally had a 'Sugar Crush' and saw the little fish boosters clearing away the candy. I love those fish. With over 400 levels, I could potentially be playing this game the rest of my life - especially if I don't make any purchases or share with Facebook friends. Only time will tell if I cave-in and make a purchase. King did a great job with this free game...maybe I owe them at least a couple of in-app purchases.<br /><br />I don't play many games like this. I usually go for word games & puzzles. So when I was stumped,  I did an internet search & learned that I didn't need to match 3 candies all the time, but had other options available. (Using the '?' in the menu will give you some info too.) I learned how to make striped candies, wrapped candies, & color bombs  & how to use them. For example, 2 striped candies together will clear horizontal or vertical columns according to which way the stripes run. I'll probably do a few more internet searches as I progress through the levels.<br /><br />I'm glad I finally gave in & tried this game. You get 5 life's to start and if you run out then you either have to PAY for more, ask your friends on Facebook to send you some life, or wait a certain amount of time for one life (you get one life every so often and max out at 5). Also, you have to PAY AGAIN for more power-ups. Some levels will take you FOREVER to beat unless you either have power-ups or once again, PAY for extra moves. So basically, unless you have a lot of money, friends that don't mind you sending them a ridiculous amount of requests (and them responding), or don't mind waiting around a half hour for one life after you run out, then you have an extremely small percentage of advancing very far in the game. Now this game would be very fun if you could EARN power-ups, tickets (some areas require you to have tickets to advance which you can PAY for or have FB friends send them), and lives. Here are some things to consider:<br /><br />Get a Facebook Game Only profile! I You can create a drama-less profile by not adding any personal info, add a handful of anonymous people from the Candy Crush Facebook fan page looking for people to friend them. There are also groups and fan pages devoted to people wanting Facebook friends just for games (there are literally hundreds to thousands of people looking for people to add them as friends so they can get lives and free goodies in games that couldn't care less about FB, drama or you personally). Then sync your apps to your Facebook page. If you do this you probably won't ever have to go back to your Facebook page unless you want to add more people or you want to play on your computer. Set up a free Gmail account if your afraid of being spammed or hacked and only use it for your Facebook. Free Facebook, Free Email, Free Game, Free Friends and almost endless lives/free tickets!<br /><br />or<br /><br />Link it to your existing Facebook Profile. That is what I have done and I have a ton of people who play also. You can choose whom you request help from unlike some games. On the Facebook app there is even a choice to request lives from people who are already playing the game. All it takes are three good friends that play a couple times a week at least to help unlock levels. Lives will build up over time so truthfully as long as people are helping you progress with tickets you don't have to spend any money to advance. My husband and I can sit here passing lives back and forth between us for as long as we want to play. As far as I know their is no request limits from any one person.<br /><br />and<br /><br />Install the app on multiple devices! If you have a Kindle, smart phone and computer then you already have 15 lives to start with aside from what friends send you. You'll also find that a level that seems impossible to beat on one device is easier to manage on another device. Many cheat sites will say use computer/FB app to complete or use tablet/phone app to win. Every app on each device will build it's own lives up without affecting each other so I could use my smartphone lives, then my tablet, then my computer and by the time I get back to my phone I have a few lives built back up and so on.<br /><br />and<br /><br />Download a couple other Games like Candy Crush where life builds up and sync to your Facebook. When you have your Facebook set up all you have to do with your other games is download to your device and sync to your Facebook.<br /><br />If you think the above is a hassle then just suck it up and pay to play. I generally enjoy this game.  It is essentially a quirky game similar to bejeweled where you match up different colored types of candy into rows of various sizes to clear maps of different sizes and configurations.  Some are timed, others have unique obstacles and others have a limited amount of moves.  It is entertaining and relaxing in that you have to think about the moves you are going to make and consider how it might effect the board, but it can be frustrating at times because the candy is always set randomly so there is a truly random chance of passing a level each time.<br /><br />I took one star off, however, for two reasons:<br /><br />First, the music.  I suppose it is supposed to kind of sound like a carnival or something a little bit, but what it mostly sounds like to me is a badly out of tune piano being banged on by a circus chimp.  It is always slightly off key, repetitive and plays in an infinite loop until it kind of stutters then starts over from the top.  Normally I just turn it off and play my own music which is the exact opposite of Bejeweled (which this game obviously is patterned after) where the music is bewitching and truly relaxing.  Like I said, probably a style choice to be kind of carnival sounding, but I would leave any carnival that kept playing that ridiculous gonging.<br /><br />Second, gated content.  This game is free and that always means that you can except some level of trickery/deceit/slash annoying hurdle to slow you down and annoy you.  We all know it and accept it, but it is one of the things I detest the most about &#34;free&#34; games.  To start with, this game randomly distributes things onto the board and this dramatically effects your chances of clearing any given level.  In addition, you only get so many &#34;lives&#34; and recharges of those are on a timer so if you expend them too quickly you may have to wait 30 minutes to get another.  That is, unless you are willing to buy one for real money OR go to Facebook andbegin trolling your friends to give you one like a beggar in a Charles Dickens novel.  Personally I just use that time to move on to something more productive, but that's not the end of the designer's circle of frustration.  As you clear levels you encounter a mini-story which is a nonsensical tale about various candy based creatures wanting you to give them candy (wouldn't that make them cannibals?) to traverse to a new area of levels.  So pretty much an endless treadmill path of levels, but at various points it stops you and requires you to pass &#34;special bonus levels&#34; in order to travel to the next area.  And once again you have one of three options;  play and pass the levels, pay real money for your &#34;free&#34; game or broadcast to all your Facebook buddies that you play this game and beg them to stop their lives and help you pass a level.  If you opt for the &#34;play and pass the level&#34; option though you can only pass one level every 24 hours locking you into a minimum 72 hour tollgate which could be longer if you keep getting a poor random draw of candies that stop you from being able to pass one for awhile.<br /><br />To be honest, the first time I ran into this gated situation I almost just deleted the whole thing because I think the whole system is a joke and I don't like encouraging them to keep doing it rather than just charging me $5 or whatever up front and letting me go, but I stuck it out, passed the levels, waited the time etc, but they just keep popping up every 10 levels or so and its annoying.  I would also warn you that if your child is going to play this game I would suggest that you make certain they can't buy anything without your permission or you just may find that they have bought $20 worth of &#34;candy&#34; trying to get through this thing.<br /><br />Bottom line its a good game and I do enjoy it, but the music is baffling/disturbing and the intentionally gated content and incessant attempts to strong-arm you into spendingreal money like a sailor on shore leave in Bangkok is nearly intolerable.  This game is good enough to pay $5 or $10 for, but the devious ploy to drain unlimited money out of the players with shameful tactics is bad enough to make me consider deleting it at least once a week.  My 2 cents is don't pay them a nickel for anything and consider it a challenge to just roll with whatever obstacle they toss in your way.

If it takes numerous tries to reach the next level, either keep on playing until you get it right, or pay small amounts to buy additional helps like special candy bombs or lollipop hammers for a buck or three. There are two issues one runs into in these so-called free games, If you feel compelled to reach the next level right this minute, the small amounts paid for 'helps' can get costly. I spent $9.00 in two weeks to purchase extra 'helps' to reach higher levels. I'm not going to do that again. I read a review where a person spent $230 in one month. Yikes! The other issue is waiting for 'lives' that you need if you want to play for free, which can range between a few minutes to as long as 24 hours. Hey, it's a game, just don't get addicted.

I have tried numerous puzzle games, yet keep coming back to Candy Crush Saga.  It is fun and really can become quite addicting.<br /><br />Visuals:<br /><br />The graphics are detailed and high-quality.  Colors are vibrant and enhance the playing experience.  One minor annoyance is that this app seems to cause my screen to flicker on occasion, mainly with the auto-brightness turned on.  It does not last forever, nor occur all of the time, so not enough to negatively impact play.<br /><br />Sound:<br /><br />There are options to turn the sound and music on/off by tapping in the lower left corner of your screen.  I find the music and sound effects to be very well done, without being overwhelming. The music reminds me of what you would hear on an old Merry-Go-Round.<br /><br />Battery/Resource/Memory Usage:<br /><br />This game uses a lot of memory, but has not affected the performance of my Kindle HDX, thus far.  Even when I am not actually playing, it uses 135MB of RAM.  For comparison, the next closest app uses 39MB.<br /><br />It also seems to draw a lot of battery power.  On my Kindle HDX, playing this game for about 30 min can move the indicator from full to about 82% or so, depending on the level set.<br /><br />Neither of these has caused a performance loss nor affected my decision to continue playing.  I enjoy the game too much and, for me, they are minor inconveniences. I mention them to provide information for those who may consider these factors a major influence.<br /><br />Game-play:<br /><br />Candy Crush Saga is very fun to play.  The lower levels slowly introduce you to how the game works and also allow you to try out some of the power-ups for free.  You can tell if a free one is available on the start screen as there will be a number on the icon. Also, as you play, you discover how to combine candies to create more powerful ones.<br /><br />The game gives you five lives, at a time, for free.  Once you use those up it is about 17 minutes until you will get another life and about an hour until full.  You can choose to have the game notify you, or just wait it out.  While I do wish there were one or two more standard lives, I think five is satisfactory for a free game.  Additionally, using them up provides a break from playing.<br /><br />The levels, in general, fall into a few categories: &#34;Clear all of the Jelly, Bring Ingredients down to the bottom, Score so many points in so many moves, and Score so many points in a certain amount of time.&#34;  As you progress through different level sets, new challenges are thrown at you, such as &#34;caged&#34; candies, chocolate that moves and blocks out squares, and bombs to &#34;defuse.&#34;<br /><br />Candy Crush has done a very nice job of inter-mixing degrees of difficulty.  I would not say it is always progressively harder, yet as you move further along, strategy plays a larger part.  Of course, there are some levels that can be frustrating, yet when you beat them, it is a nice sense of accomplishment.<br /><br />Lastly, the game scores you using a three-star system; bronze, silver, and gold.  While I waited for new level sets to open up (explained further down), I would go back and try to hit gold on older ones.<br /><br />Ads:<br /><br />There are no ads for other products or games in Candy Crush Saga that I have noticed.  It will occasionally ask you if you want to purchase additional power ups or more moves, yet I did not find it spammy.<br /><br />Free or Pay To Win?:<br /><br />Before you start each level, the screen offers you choices of power-ups you can pay for, if you choose.  While I did try out the free ones in the early levels, I have yet to purchase any power-ups.  Currently I am on level 125 and can say that, at least up to this point, every level can be beaten without buying anything.  Some may take you longer to figure out, but I like the challenge of it.  They offer you the choice to spend money, yet do not force it.<br /><br />Also, I have not paid to unlock any new level sets.  At first, I thought that it was like the rest, and once you did the first few levels, it would cost money. I hit level 10 and the screen showed &#34;To unlock more levels.&#34; so I was initially bummed.  Having not hit gold on each one, I went back and kept playing until I scored, mostly, gold stars<br /> from 1-10.  Within a few days, the notification screen on my Kindle had something from Candy Crush Saga.  It had the icon and read &#34;The Tooth Fairy has a surprise for you.&#34; Upon opening the game, the next level set was unlocked. This has been the case for every level set up to my current level 125.  Whether or not having mostly gold stars influences it, I do not know, because I always use the time to go back and improve my scores. Be aware that the time it takes for the tooth fairy to visit can vary; sometimes a day, sometimes a few days.<br /><br />Therefore, while you have the option to spend money to progress faster, to make levels easier, it is not required.  As I mentioned, I am currently on level 125, and have not spent money.  I actually feel a little guilty about that, because this is a fun game and the developers did an excellent job designing it.  I do not think I would buy power-ups, because I enjoy the challenge of beating levels without them.  However, if it becomes the case that I have to pay to unlock levels later on, to me it would be worth it.<br /><br />Conclusion:<br /><br />I really enjoy playing Candy Crush Saga.  It is a nice break and provides challenging and fun entertainment. If you are looking for a candy/gem/balloon type game, I recommend giving this one a try.  Just be warned, it can be addicting.id to unlock any new level sets.  At first, I thought that it was like the rest, and once you did the first few levels, it would cost money. I'm no longer sure if I'm having fun or if I'm addicted. They give you little tastes in the starter levels to make you think it's fun and you're good at it. Then as the levels progress and you're burning through your 5 lives you start to question why you're even doing this. In the spirit of true addiction it offers to let you buy more or have your friends enable you. When you get stuck on a level for days or weeks at a time all you can think about is getting to that next level. Your life begins to fall apart. Things you once loved become sources of anger for you. More than once the phrase &quot;i hate chocolate!&quot; will come out of your mouth. You find yourself crushing during social events. You'll even start to surround yourself with fellow crushers. When friends aren't playing you try to talk them into it saying it's so much fun. Deep down you know you're not doing them any favors. Misery loves company. When you wake up first thing in the morning you get excited for the 5 New lives. After you run through those you're sad and watching the little crying heart until you have just one more life. It's a vicious circle, friends. Unless you're willing to devote valuable hours to this game, do yourself a favor and move on. It will consume you.

I see a lot of comments about not getting quest updates.  This is how it worked for me......<br /><br />You can not be connected to Facebook so you have to log out in the candy crush menu.<br /><br />When you get to the bridge at the end of the set of levels, select it as you were going to play a level.<br /><br />You will then see the options to play three (3) quests.  You must pass a  quest to earn a \\"key\\".<br /><br />You are only allowed to play & complete one (1) quest in a 24 hour period.  After three (3) successful quest completions, you will be forwarded to the next set of levels.<br /><br />Although this method works, it can take a long time because of the 3 days it takes to complete the 3 quests.  If you sync your device to a Facebook account, friends can give you free tickets and it is much faster.  Otherwise this method will work and it won't cost you a penny!<br /><br />That's how it worked for me and now I'm in the 300s so hope this works for you too.  Good Luck.

...otherwise you may not put this game down!  I don't know why it's so addicting (maybe they put something in the candy).  I also don't know what the saga is all about - I just know I feel terrible when I've made that little girl cry!<br /><br />Basically, this is a game of strategy in which you try to clear the board (or some similar task) in order to continue to the next level.  You do this by moving pieces of candy into groups that &quot;crush&quot;.  A somewhat creepy voice will give you encouragement when you make a particularly good move. First of all... GREAT GAME!  Now for the reason for only 1 star.  I would actually give this game 0 stars if I could.  I do NOT like playing a game where you only play so many levels and then have to wait for more lives.  Or be prompted to BUY more lives or even worse... be a nuisance to Facebook friends.  I do have Facebook, but I still won't bug my friends.  Nothing is more annoying to me than to log in to Facebook and have the whole page littered with &#34;so and so likes this game&#34; or &#34;so and so needs more ..... will you help them?&#34; But there are people out there who do not Facebook, and then what are those people supposed to do?  The only option they have then is to BUY more lives.  This is annoying as obviously the further into the game you get the more challenging it gets so therefore the more lives you use.  This game could get mighty expensive in a hurry!  Which is exactly what they want, I'm sure.  :)  With that said... I DO LIKE THE GAME!  Just not the pesky spending $$ for more lives and I will NOT be a pest on Facebook.  Now, I was willing to just suffer with the running out of lives and wait my time allotted for more lives and just silently complain to myself UNTIL I got to a certain level and then I could not advance any further on Facebook OR my Kindle.  I was STUCK at that point (I think it's level 35??)  BUT ... I could spend more $$ to advance (go figure) OR bug my Facebook friends (imagine that!) OR play a mystery level (pass of course) but then I had to wait 24 hours to unlock the next mystery level!  I am not certain how many mystery levels I would have to pass to get the next leg of the journey unlocked... and I really don't care.  At that point, I got frustrated enough to just be done with the whole game.  This ROBS all the joy out of playing a game.  I DO realize that this is one of the most popular games out there... it has a HUGE rating.  And I myself LOVE the game... but at the same time... DESPISE the game.  I hate being bothered for money and I hate bugging people on Facebook over the sake of a game.  I would RATHER buy the game for a set price and be done with it, and then be free to play the game all the way through with no more being prompted to spend money for this or that (power-ups for example) and no more being stopped at levels.  Just play all the way through.  People that keep playing this game must have spent a fortune, and I am just not willing to do that.  There are plenty of other games that are reasonably priced or even FREE that are just as much fun and WAY less stressful because they don't prompt you for money or send you to Facebook to bug people there.  If KING (makers of Candy Crush Saga) would miraculously listen to the small minority out there who feel this way and offer a paid version of this game without the prompts for Facebook or money... I will be one of the first ones to pounce on it.  Until then, I have deleted it from Facebook and my Kindle and will not play it anymore.  :(

I had it on my phone and now on my Kindle - with a nice big screen to see it!<br /><br />Anybody that doesn't know what Candy Crush is by now [I figure I'm one of the later people to get hooked], it's a game of matching same candies in threes.  Three red candies in a row or column makes them disappear.  Each little game has a goal [a certain amount of points, getting rid of &#34;gels&#34;] and it gradually gets harder so you can learn what is wanted/needed.  If you line up more than 3 like-candies, you can create a new candy with special powers, like eliminating an entire row.  If you don't get a level, you just get more tries.  Eventually, I think it decides you [okay, me] are too stupid to get that particular screen and suddenly it's really easy.<br /><br />The only frustrating thing is when you finish a &#34;level&#34;, you have to complete 3 quests to get to the next one.  This is just three more games like the others, as far as I can tell, but the frustrating part is that you can only do one a day - unless I'm missing something.  I think you can skip them by putting it on Facebook or something, but I don't want to do that. If I still want to play, I just go back to a game that I didn't get the 3 stars for and replay that one a few times.<br /><br />I can't believe that once this game gained popularity, it remained free, so get it while it still is.  It is a lot of fun.

When I first downloaded this game, I could not stop playing it. It was challenging yet fun, and the difficulty seemed to increase gradually... but then I hit a wall, and could simply not progress without burning through my handful of accumulated power-ups. After that, I'd have to spend several days on a level trying to move up in the sugarlicious world of Candy Crush.<br /><br />Before I get into the reasons as to why I'm not a fan, I'll get into the basics of the game. Levels consist of one of three goals: Score enough points, or clear the &#34;Jelly&#34; blocks, or get the &#34;ingredients&#34; to the bottom of the level. You get points/move ingredients/clear jelly blocks by matching up three like pieces of candy in either the horizontal or vertical axis. You can make certain combinations with more pieces to create special candies that have a larger area of effect. Thankfully, nothing is time-based; the challenge comes from the limited amount of turns you have combined with certain &#34;bad&#34; candies that interfere with your ability to make combos (for instance, chocolate, which will spread piece by piece every turn you don't clear a piece that is adjacent to the chocolate).<br /><br />So, why did I give up on this game? See, there are many fundamental problems with the it, and all of them are intentionally designed such so as to lead you to the store to buy the items required to advance without wasting hours trying to get the right combination.<br /><br />To begin with, the game is completely random. This is fine, it makes things more challenging and less dependent on sheer memorization. But at the same time, it gets to the point where skill takes a backseat and luck takes the wheel. You probably won't encounter this for the first several dozen missions, when you can take your time and apply strategy. Keep playing, though, and you'll run into mechanics that force you to rush combinations in order to avoid tight time limits (such as levels with bombs that countdown after each turn, and which will force you to lose instantly). Try looking up YouTube walkthrough videos for the game, and you'll see the same thing that I'm describing. Even when the perfect and commonly accepted strategy is there, you'll still see how these players will fail time and time again in the videos. Imagine how frustrating it is to try to figure out how to beat a level, in any game, and then seeing that even when you're doing things right, you're still prone to losing.<br /><br />And on the topic of losing, we again find a situation where you either have to be extremely patient or extremely willing to part with your money to advance. You begin with five lives. Lose a level - lose a life. Lives are restored at the rate of one per every half hour, meaning that if you lose all five, you'll at least have to wait thirty minutes before you can try the level again. Or, you can pull out some digital currency and hop right back into the game and try again. Be warned, at the later levels, you're probably going to lose due to a lack of viable combinations.<br /><br />To be fair, you CAN wait for those lives to come back, and in a relatively short time limit. But when the lose rate becomes ridiculous, you have to start relying on power-up candies that give you an upper-hand. By the time you actually start needing these, you'll probably have at least a few saved up. But when you're done with those, the only way to get more is by winning them on the daily spin (one possible per day), or... shell out some dollars. And even THEN, using one power-up on a level may not be enough; you might need a few to clear that ridiculously and artificially difficult level.<br /><br />TL;DR: It's a fun game for a few days, but you'll get to the point where you need to either wait quite a long time, or you'll need to pay money. And in the grand scheme of things, that's what this game was designed to do: make the developers money on microtransactions for items that may or may not even secure you a victory.<br /><br />I just can't get behind that philosophy, and that's why I have to rate the game so low.

I already knew enough about Candy Crush Saga to know what I was getting into going in, and it was free, so I haven't got too much to complain about.  The basic game is similar to a huge number of other games where you connect three, four or five in a row, and try to accomplish certain tasks.  The graphics are better than most, some of the levels are tricky but most aren't too bad, at least at the beginning. The catch is that you have five lives, once you use them, you either put the game aside for a while till you get more lives, or you buy lives.  At first you actually get lives as fast as you use them, but this doesn't last all that long.  Eventually you end up hitting levels where you have to buy boosters to be able to finish the level.  The free game ends up not being free.<br /><br />If you want to pester people on facebook to give you lives, or if you are willing to pay for lives and boosters, or if you're willing to quit playing when you get tired of playing for fifteen minutes and then waiting an hour to play again, the game is entertaining.  If you're going to get extremely annoyed when they ask you if you want to buy more lives for the fiftieth time, or ask you if you want to pay $0.99 to get extra moves to finish a level because you only have two tiles remaining, then this probably isn't the game for you.

Early levels are reasonably fun and free.  Typical match 3 play with some cute twists, some using features inspired by several other games.  Many other games just as fun though, just not as well known.  Frustration slowly mounts with later rounds, once you are used to having fun (addictive).<br /><br />The game suffers from two main problems.  One is limited lives and quests.  These regulate how often you can play the game once it gets more difficult (unless you are willing to buy powerups or extra lives, then no longer free!)  Most other games don't ration turns so severely.  The other issue is the occasional &#34;rigged carnival game&#34; level.  These levels are virtually impossible to win with just &#34;skill and strategy&#34;.  Winning these levels requires extraordinary random luck to be able to make the candy combos necessary to win.  These carnival levels become more frequent the further you get in to the game and take longer to get past - until you finally give up and play something else that is fun.  Finally, a minor complaint, not all game features are always available when playing offline (e.g. Owl game)<br /><br />Four stars for competent match 3 game concept.  Deducting a few stars for carnival rigging, severely rationed free lives, quests, and &#34;needing&#34; a few more permissions than really necessary.

King.com, the company behind this game, directly lifted gameplay concepts from other games including Bejeweled as well as a previously-existing independently developed game called CandySwipe.  They then trademarked the term &#34;Candy&#34; and have aggressively gone after any other game using the word candy in its title, including the developer who had created his game BEFORE Candy Crush Saga.  They have also attempted to trademark the term &#34;Saga,&#34; and have been attempting to block release of games including that word as well, even though there is absolutely no risk of confusion.  What's more, there is nothing &#34;saga&#34; about Candy Crush, as opposed to games like The Banner Saga, an actual saga about Vikings, which they have attempted to block.<br /><br />King.com is effectively nothing more than a trademark troll company, and while this game may be addicting, it also establishes pay walls to attempt to drain money from players via microtransactions.  It is not a very good game, and it's from a terrible company, so I would urge everyone in the strongest sense to avoid this, and instead look more at games like CandySwipe.  Please don't support King.com.

More than just a fun way to kill a few minutes, I really think this game is kind of exercise for your brain. Seriously! You have to pay attention to so many different variables all at the same time- from planning your moves wisely, to keeping track of the time/moves remaining, to creating the most valuable combinations for the most points. And yet, the thrill you get when you defeat a game on the first try!<br /><br />  I noticed that a lot of the reviews don't really describe how the game is played. The concept is very simple (at first!). The easiest games, i.e., the lower levels, are usually small boards filled with rows of different colored candies. The object is to match 3 or more of the same colors in a row horizontally or vertically, but not diagonally. In this way, you move/eliminate/create candies to achieve the goal of that game. In some games the object is to accumulate a certain amount of points (sometimes these games are timed). There are games where you try to get ingredients (cherries and hazelnuts) to the bottom of the row, games where you try to eliminate certain types of -and combinations of- candies, and so on. Every level gets progressively more difficult, and introduces new boards and new hazards!<br /><br />  You'll quickly find that special candies are your best friends. Matching 4 of the same color in a row will give you a striped color candy, which when matched with 2 more of the same color will wipe out the entire row. Matching 5 candies to make a T or L shape gives you a wrapped candy, which, when combined with others of the same color, will blow up the immediately surrounding candies. Matching 5 in a row gives you what most people call a color bomb, which can eliminate any color you match it with. Best of all are the combinations; any two special candies can be combined. One of the best is combining a striped and wrapped candy (of any color) to create what I call the jelly bean of death. It will wipe out great swaths of candies, horizontally and vertically. My favorite is combining a color bomb with a striped candy. This turns every candy of that color into a striped candy and activates them all at the same time. Bliss! There are also lollipop hammers to eliminate obstacle candies and wrappers, red hands that will switch two adjacent candies, and other helpful candies.<br /><br />  You're given 5 lives at a time. Once you run out of lives by not completing the goal of that game, you can buy more or wait for them to re-accumulate (app. 1 every half hour, though I may be wrong about this). You can also buy special candies and other helpful items. Candy Crush has recently added a free daily spin-the-wheel game to win a helpful prize!<br /><br />  I really love that they haven't made it a necessity to pay to play. I personally would rather pay the full cost up front, so was kinda annoyed when I first started playing at the thought of having to pay to continue. Well, you don't have to! I decided to try and play without spending any more money, and now I'm on level 205, and I have to confess I haven't spent more than a dollar on this game yet.<br /><br />  You'll find lots of helpful hints on the internet (I REALLY recommend them) just by searching candy crush and your level number. The only thing about this game I hate? They made chocolate the bad guy!!!

It seems everyone I know is addicted to this game.<br /><br />hundreds of difficult levels to try and accomplish, and the graphics and sounds are great. Typical swap and match game, with bonus candies for matching larger numbers of candies.<br /><br />The game starts you off pretty easy and simple so you get the hang of the game.... then it starts getting harder!<br /><br />The difficulty sets in when you have to make a certain number of special candies, or swap certain numbers of those special candies, or &#34;bring fruit down&#34; before you run out of turns... sometimes there's &#34;bombs&#34; that go off after a certain number of moves unless you swap them out. You would think that chocolate that multiplies would be a good thing (I love chocolate) but in this game it's NOT a good thing!! The chocolate will cover the board and block your moves.<br /><br />Then add to all those &#34;specials&#34; the interesting game board configurations, some with portals to other sections of the board.<br /><br />Relatively recently they've added an additional game set with the owl... more addiction!! In the owl games, you have to eliminate equal numbers of 2 colors, or the crescent moon the owl is sitting on tips (like a scale) and the owl falls off.. and you lose that game.<br /><br />It's no wonder this game is played by so many people... it's very entertaining, challenging, and fun!

Candy Crush is super addictive. If you have better things to do, don't even get started. But if you have extra time on your hands, you will absolutely love the challenge and the competition... you can easily see the progression through levels and compare to your other family and friends who are also playing.
As match 3 gameplay goes, you match 3 of a kind together to gain points. Candy crush saga takes this to a new level by adding many special abilities and objectives. If this was a game on a dedicated game console, it would easily overshadow the old games like Bejeweled. Unfortunately, the gameplay gets overly chaotic and difficult very quickly. This wouldn't be a problem, as I like difficult games such as Super Meat Boy and the Bit.trip series, but if you fail a level, you lose a life. The only way to get lives is by waiting half an hour. Worse yet, the lives max out at 5, so you can't hoard lives. The gameplay can become increasingly luck based, as candies are generated randomly in each level, meaning if you restart a level, you might get a slightly more forgiving arrangement, but each time you restart, you lose a life. Once you lose all your lives, you cannot play any levels, including past ones. It basically blocks you off the game until half an hour passes. So you can either wait half an hour and try again, or you can PAY to refill your life meter. This game is not the only mobile game guilty of overfishing IAPs, but this game asks you to buy something so frequently, it drops my rating of this app from 5 stars to 2. I say it would be better on a console because a console's game is not just there to make a quick buck by ripping off customers, for they focus on a strong experience. I'm sorry, but a game that begs for money so much probably wasn't designed to be fun, but to make money. In the end, a strong, innovative game is ruined by IAPs.

This game is not suitable for children, because it constantly asks for money (although some games are much worse).  You only get five lives, and when those expire you must buy more for 99 cents each time, or wait half an hour to regenerate a single life. Other game boosters are also for sale. That means you can only play for a few minutes, then must pay again and again to play more, unless you put the game away for two hours and come back to it (and no child is going to want to do that).  So this game can get awfully expensive extremely quickly.  Games should be completely free or they should sell them at a set price, and not try to take unfair advantage of children.  Otherwise, the game itself is one of the better match three games.

I've played candy crush for 6 months and can safely say I'm addicted.  At first it was a lot of fun so I've played up to level 140.  Along the way I found  the game is full of flaws, some of them seem on purpose.  It won't let you win certain levels; levels so hard, it's impossible to win without buying an assist or two.  The game is geared up to get you to buy stuff.  I play without buying anything.  Have been stuck on a level as long as a month.  It gives you free game assists, then it takes them back by not allowing you to use them -- example:  I was surprised with 50 free gold bars but after I used 3 or 4, they started disappearing--5 to 10 at a time.  I'd turn my tablet on and find the bars decreased from 40 to 34; then from 21 to 14.  Used 2 more and it went down to 5.  It won't let me use the 5.  The game encourages you to open Facebook and beg your friends who play candy crush to send you lives and extra moves, but then it seldom lets you use the lives and extra moves you receive.  When you run out of lives and try to apply them, your gifts disappear but don't get applied to your game.  That's just two of the many, many frustrating programming flaws.  I have read lots of complaints on line about this and other problems with candy crush but King Corporation won't respond with an explanation or fix the flaws.  I still play for free only but only because it's a real challenge, not because it's fun.

Abandon hope, all who enter the King-dom. Candy Crush is fun, challenging, and yes, addictive. It's also frustrating, infuriating, enervating, and even demoralizing. I'd play more often and ultimately spend about the same if the game had two modifications that allowed me to play on my own terms.<br /><br />First, I'd like to &#34;Undo&#34; a move. You may see your error the instant you muscle twitches, but you cannot reverse the move. Second, when a level proves too difficult, I'd like to be able simply to check out of it. Now, you must continue to struggle with it, becoming more inept with every attempt. Occasionally a long break (weeks, not hours) will allow you to succeed when you return refreshed, and occasionally sufficient repetitions will bring up a board that will make success inevitable. In general, your choice is continue to drive yourself crazy or spend, spend, spend.<br /><br />So although I enjoy playing Candy Crush, and my circuitry like that of every other player celebrates when I triumph, I basically resent the underlying model of extortion that requires you to buy your way out of prolonged suffering.

The original game is way better than a.y of its imitators. It is incredibly addictive as the levels are mixed difficulty rather than each getting harder. The in app purchasing used to be not so expensive, but there is now a huge leap in price between a 99 set of 5 lives to the next price of $5.99 do 50 lives. Before it wasn't a big deal to get a set of lives to get that last bit to win a level, but when the price goes up by $5.00 for the next bunch of lives, it's time to 're-examine exactly what you are buying. In the end you have nothing but a bill for literally $50 dollars or more for a few seconds of time. PARENTS!! YOU BETTER SET THE PARENTAL CONTROLS OR YOUR MORTGAGE MONEY WILL BE GOING TO KING!!! I have four kids, and I could easily see them racking up a bunch without even realizing it. Sometimes, it's even hard for me, and I should know better. This new pricing scheme really disappoints me, especially as a loyal fan and player. There are certainly enough levels to have made tons of money off of the impatient and frenzied players; the needs, more expensive pricing structure as well as the many clones made by King itself have revealed just how greedy the developers are. So, play, have a great time, but beware of the in app buying. It's not as sweet as candy!

I really wish I could have rated five stars to this game. But there are to many flaws for me to keep liking this one. The app is free to download, but if you want too proceed in the game, even if is by just a few levels, must pay to proceed playing. Either that or you can play mystery quests (really levels you'd already completed), and wait THREE DAYS before you can keep playing. The game gives you only five lives, and then it times you out for nearly 3 hours to get a full set of lives again. Unless you pay for it! Yep, this game really is a money maker off of impatient players. Don't fall for this scam! Once you pay ridiculously high prices with golden bars, you pay with real money, and don't stop.The game is actually pretty challenging and fun, but there are so may other games out there, like the original game Candy Swipe (that you pay one price and it is completely free), and the Jewl games such as Bejewled and Dragon Gem that let you play for free. This game wants you to keep paying for lives, boosters, and tickets to win thier games. But players don't really notice that the levels are based on luck, and it can take you days to beat.The company has copyrighted the words &amp;#34;Candy&amp;#34; and &amp;#34;Saga&amp;#34;, and uses other game developers on the market for thier titles even if they came way before this game. If a game will time you out after you've used lives that are each gone in like one or two minutes, I don't really want to play this game.<br /><br /> ..

Five Stars? One Star?<br /><br />Talk about a Love/Hate relationship. The game is addictive, and my wife, my six year old grandson and I (especially me) have a difficult time not playing when we should be asleep, but for one more chance. That's the Love side. The Hate side comes later when I have to wake up, make breakfast and take my grandson to school. I suffer from a sugar hangover from finally turning it off at 2:00 a.m.<br /><br />The game does have its redeeming features requiring greater planning and understanding as I progress from level to level, building on what came before. There are strategies that evolve and continue to make the game interesting and not boring like many games.<br /><br />My only criticism is that as an adult, I'm able to resist spending a buck for five more moves. Don't let your teenager have access to your credit card or this game could become expensive.

Addictive! **Warning #1**  You can't play this game for a few minutes! Time will fly by and before you know it, you are late for work! I suggest you set a timer before starting the game. It is incredibly fun and entertaining and it makes you compete against the cute characters to move up levels. **Warning #2** do not let anyone play the game for you to help you! Playing the game is like going to school, every thing you learn to get you through that level, you will need to know to help you through the next level (or future levels)! Trust me on that, I let my neice play for me, and I was forced to uninstall and reinstall to start over because I needed to know what little tricks she learned on previous levels to pass to the next level. Yes there are tricks to learn, and you will also learn or improve multi-tasking skills as well. As your playing, your watching the candy with the timer, making calculated moves, busting the bubbles and keeping a check on your remaining moves left! The game will outsmart you and frustrate you while your determined to beat it. You will compete with family and friends and spend hours in this love/hate relationship with Candy Crush. This is a great, no correction, it's a brilliant game!

I have played some bad games before.  They usually fell between so poorly programmed they were more frustrating than fun or so over-engineered you spend more time reading about it than actually playing it.  There is new catagory that lies between the two fore mentioned points that is called &#34;pay to play&#34; or &#34;pay to win&#34;.<br /><br />Candy Crush Saga is  simple puzzle game that in addition to featuring the &#34;match three to clear&#34; it also diverges gameplay with other objectives like clearing particular candies, guiding other candies to the bottom of the screen, etc within limited moves.  The screen lights-up with fireworks and cheers with every successful match and subsequent chains!  I can understand why so many people are addicted to this!<br /><br />Being the jaded player, I figured out pretty quick what was going on.  Initially providing simple challenges on par with Tetris, the difficultly are so slowly increased that buying into the game becomes the only way to keep up the gamer's high.  It sounds neferous but in some odd way, I kind of respect the developers ingenuity to exploilt the casual gamers sense of perseverance and and self-satisfaction!<br /><br />With that in mind, BEWARE!  Its a fun game but the pay to play and ultimately win  model seriously destorts what makes theses casual game fun.  Far be it to tell you how to spend your money, but you can buy so much more experiences  than any in-game purchase offered

The first few levels are fun and relaxing. Sadly, there are sections where King wants you to fail. They give you a certain amt of lives to accomplish each objective.  If you fail and have no more lives the choices are simple:  Get one from a friend that has one to spare, wait 9 minutes for the life timer to reset, or play something else and come back to Candy Crush later.  Naturally, King hopes pride &amp; impatience kick in so that you open your wallet to buy more lives. (You certainly can't let anyone know you failed!)  Yes, it costs money to develop and offer these so-called free games,  but even the free ones can get rather expensive.  I was certainly glad I play off-line because a few times I would tap something that did not initially say was a cash purchase within the game.  The choices on the screen look like you earn game credits that can be redeemed for lives,  etc.  When it comes to the objective to clear all the jellies you frequently have to go over the same ones multiple times for them to clear.  It is easy to fail the level because, again, you have limited moves.  The &quot;free&quot; portion of Candy Crush is the first 35 levels.  I did not see this info when i initially installed it.  All other levels must be purchased.  To summarize, the reasons for a rating of 4 out of 5 are these:  When you install the game it states you have an option to make in-app purchases, but does not indicate what they are until the moment of choosing or denying one.  The instructions are minimal.  Since King Company wants players to be online w/ Facebook they need to supply a way to turn off the purchase option so nothing is accidentally purchased or tell players to &quot;Play Safe- Play Offline.&quot;  When it comes to &quot;Clear the Jellies&quot; they should provide in the instructions that the same jellies must somehow be blasted 3 times each.  Don't make people figure these things out via game losses. Finally, let people know that only the first 35 levels are free.  The gamers set up the game that way. No one should have to read through public reviews for that or other info.  Will I be purchasing further levels?  Nope.  I am deleting the game for a new one today.
